anomalies.observed: On the root sheet the Tag-Connect SWD header J2 carries global labels SWDIO (pin 2) = NET0011, SWCLK (pin 4) = NET0012 and SWO (pin 6) = NET0006. The same labels appear on the MCU U2 right-hand column at PB13 (NET0011), PB14 (NET0012) and PB3 (NET0006). Those very PB13/PB14 wires are the ones that run from the DISPLAY sheet symbol (child hierarchical labels NET0002 = DISP_SDA on U3 D1/D2, NET0019 = DISP_SCL on U3 D0). Thus the SWD programming data/clock lines are merged onto the same MCU pins as the OLED I2C bus, and SWO is on PB3 instead of the trace pin.
anomalies.expected: The spec states J1's pins are 'VCC, GND, ~{RESET}, SWCLK, SWDIO, SWO - a standard ARM debug/programming interface, not a user I/O', and separately places the display bus on PB12/PB13/PB14 (DISP_SCL on PB13, DISP_SDA on PB14). The SWDIO/SWCLK/SWO lines must connect to the MCU's dedicated debug pins (PA13/PA14/PA15), not to the display I2C pins, so the debug interface and the display bus must remain separate nets.

anomalies.impact: The SWD debug/programming bus and the OLED I2C bus share the same MCU pins (PB13/PB14). Programming the MCU would drive/short the display SDA/SCL lines, and normal display operation would toggle the SWDIO/SWCLK nets, preventing reliable SWD flashing and corrupting the display bus; SWO on PB3 also fails to provide trace output on the expected pin.
